answers.answer: Reveal the top region card and put the King there; each player takes another region card as their home region and places their Grande there. Of ten initial Caballeros, put two in the home region beside the Grande, one on the first success-track space, and seven in the court.
answers.evidence: Setup: ‘reveal the top card and put the King in that region’; two home, one track, seven court.

answers.answer: In round 1, players choose the starter. In later rounds, the player who took the last turn in the preceding round starts. Others play clockwise. No power-card value already played that round may be matched.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, step 2: chosen starter; later, last-turn player begins; others clockwise; no value already played may be matched.

answers.answer: Players take turns in descending power-card value. At the start of the turn, recruit up to the Caballero allowance shown on the power card from provinces into court; then choose an available action card.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, steps 3–4: ‘descending power-card value’; ‘At the start of your turn recruit’; ‘After recruitment, choose’.

answers.answer: If your provinces lack enough of your color, you may take your own Caballeros from the board to make up the difference. The King’s region and Castillo cannot supply pieces: the King’s region is taboo, and the Castillo cannot supply pieces outside general scoring.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, step 3: may take own from board; King’s region remains taboo and Castillo cannot supply pieces outside general scoring.

answers.answer: Ordinary deployment moves up to the action-card number from your court to regions adjacent to the King’s current region and/or the Castillo; the allowance may be divided freely. It is a maximum, so you may deploy fewer or none. The stated rule does not prohibit splitting among destinations.
answers.evidence: Ordinary deployment: ‘maximum’; ‘Move them from your court to any regions adjacent ... and/or the Castillo, dividing the allowance freely.’

answers.answer: Yes. Complete ordinary deployment and the special action in either order, but finish one before starting the other; neither may be split or interleaved. The special action may be declined.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, step 4: ‘Do them in either order’; ‘neither may be split or interleaved’; ‘You may decline the special action’.

answers.answer: After a turn, lay the selected action card aside so later players cannot choose it. After all players turn, discard remaining face-up action cards. The King card is revealed each round and is never permanently discarded.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, step 5: selected card laid aside; remaining face-up cards discarded after all turns; King card ‘never permanently discarded’.

answers.answer: No Caballero, Grande, or mobile scoreboard may move into or out of the King’s region; special actions do not override this. The region may still be scored. Moving the King changes which region is protected.
answers.evidence: Protected locations: ‘no Caballero, Grande or mobile scoreboard may move into or out of it’; ‘It may still be scored’; moving the King changes protected region.

answers.answer: Clearly announce how many Caballeros enter the Castillo. They may enter regardless of the King’s location. They cannot be removed by an action and leave only during general scoring.
answers.evidence: Protected locations: ‘Announce clearly how many’; ‘regardless of the King’s location’; leave ‘only during general scoring’.

answers.answer: General scoring occurs after rounds 3, 6, and 9. In order: (1) each player secretly sets a disk to one board region other than the King’s region for all their Castillo pieces, before the Castillo is uncovered; (2) uncover and score the Castillo; (3) reveal disks and move each player’s Castillo pieces to that one destination, except pieces whose destination is the King’s region go to their owner’s court, then replace the Castillo empty; (4) score the nine regions in scoring-track order. Destinations are chosen before revealing the Castillo.
answers.evidence: General scoring: four ordered stages; stage 1 says destinations selected ‘before uncovering the Castillo’.

answers.answer: A player cannot split their Castillo Caballeros or leave any in the Castillo: all of that player’s pieces go to one chosen destination, and the Castillo is emptied. The destination choice excludes the King’s region. If pieces are directed to the King’s region, they go to that player’s court instead.
answers.evidence: General scoring stages 1 and 3: ‘all ... must go to one region’; selected King’s region sends pieces to court; none may be retained or split.

answers.answer: The three players tied at four each score 3 points apiece, and the player with three scores 1. Grandes do not count toward majority; only Caballeros count.
answers.evidence: Example: 5/3/1 with counts 4,4,4,3 scores 3,3,3,1; ‘A Grande ... contributes zero Caballeros.’

answers.answer: The player with four scores 6; the player with three scores 4; both players with two score 0.
answers.evidence: Publisher example: 6/4/2, counts 4,3,2,2 score 6,4,0,0.

answers.answer: In a two-player game, only first place can pay; in a three-player game, first and second can pay. A tie for first in a two-player game shifts to second place, which is outside the payable ranks, so neither scores.
answers.evidence: Region ranks: two players only first; three players first and second; ‘a two-player tie for first pays neither player’.

answers.answer: Whenever the relevant region is scored, including special scoring, the sole majority holder in the King’s region gets +2, and the sole majority holder with their own Grande in that region gets +2. Neither bonus is awarded on a tie for first.
answers.evidence: Bonuses apply ‘whenever ... scored, including special scorings’; both bonuses +2 for sole majority; neither on tie.

answers.answer: Special Castillo scoring does not empty it or redistribute pieces. Uncover and score the Castillo, then cover the same Caballeros again; redistribution waits for general scoring.
answers.evidence: Stack 3 Castillo: ‘score it, then put the Castillo over the same Caballeros; redistribution waits until general scoring’.

answers.answer: A mobile scoreboard may be introduced from beside the board or moved from one region to a different region; the Castillo is allowed. It cannot move into or out of the King’s region. The two scoreboards cannot be stacked, and they must remain right side up as 8/4/0 or 4/0/0, not rotated or reversed.
answers.evidence: Stack 4 Mobile scoreboard: introduce or move; Castillo allowed; King-region movement forbidden; cannot stack; never reversed or rotated.

answers.answer: Move your Grande to another region, but not into the King’s region or Castillo; it cannot leave the King’s region. The destination may already contain several Grandes. The destination becomes your new home region.
answers.evidence: Stack 4 Grande: restrictions, destination may contain several Grandes, and ‘destination becomes your new home region’.

answers.answer: Return any one of your played power cards to your hand, including the card played this turn. You need not reveal which; taking the visible top card will of course be apparent.
answers.evidence: Stack 4 Power Cards: ‘any one ... including the one played this turn’; ‘need not reveal which’.

answers.answer: The game ends after all stages of the third general scoring, after round 9. The player furthest along the success track wins. No additional endgame tiebreaker is given.
answers.evidence: End: ‘Finish all stages of the third general scoring, after round 9’; furthest along wins.

answers.answer: Separate action cards into stacks by the 1–5 Caballeros printed on their backs, shuffle each stack separately, and place face down. Reveal the top card of each of five stacks at the start of each round. The standard round marker starts at 1.
answers.evidence: Setup: sort and shuffle each stack; standard round marker starts at 1. Turn Structure: reveal top card of each of five stacks.

answers.answer: Played power cards do not return to hand automatically; they remain in each player’s face-up used stack, with only the top card visible. A special action can recover a played card.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: played cards remain in face-up used stack, ‘only the top card visible’; special action can recover one.

answers.answer: If the King is moved before ordinary deployment, the King’s new position determines adjacent destinations; if deployment happens first, use his old position. The King card can place him in any region except the Castillo.
answers.evidence: Protected locations gives old/new position timing; Stack 5: King in ‘any region except Castillo’.

answers.answer: Take and retain the Veto card before you to stop one special action during the current or next round. It cannot stop the ordinary deployment part of an action card.
answers.evidence: Stack 2 Veto: ‘Put the card before you and retain it’; stop one special action; ‘cannot stop the ordinary deployment portion’.

answers.answer: While you hold Veto, other players must announce special actions before executing them. Object as soon as the player starts: you can stop an announced action before execution or stop the remaining part of an incomplete action. A completed action cannot be vetoed; parts already executed are not undone, and you may prevent just part.
answers.evidence: Veto description specifies announcement, object timing, incomplete/complete action treatment, and no undo of executed parts.

answers.answer: Discard Veto after using it once. If unused, discard it at the end of the next round.
answers.evidence: Veto: ‘Discard after using the veto once; if unused, discard at the end of the next round.’

answers.answer: Every fellow player, but not the selecting player, sends all Caballeros in their court to the provinces. An empty court sends none.
answers.evidence: Decay of Authority—all court: every fellow player sends all court Caballeros to provinces; empty court sends none; selecting player unaffected.

answers.answer: The fellow player with two sends both to the provinces because they send all they have if fewer than three. The selecting player is unaffected, so their five remain in court.
answers.evidence: Decay—three from court: ‘three ... or all they have if fewer than three’; selecting player unaffected.

answers.answer: The detailed execution paragraph and matching card require each player, including the selecting player, to return three of their own Caballeros to the provinces. Starting with the selecting player’s left neighbor, proceed clockwise, and the selecting player acts last. Each chooses pieces from any regions and/or their court, never the King’s region or Castillo. No shortfall procedure is supplied if fewer than three eligible pieces exist. The heading says ‘fellow players,’ unlike the detailed paragraph and card face.
answers.evidence: The King returns paragraph states all players, three own, left then clockwise and selector last, source restrictions; heading discrepancy noted.

answers.answer: The selecting player chooses one Caballero from a region for each player, including themselves, and returns each to its owner’s provinces. No pieces may be taken from courts, the King’s region, or Castillo. The summary does not provide a fallback if a player has no eligible piece.
answers.evidence: Send one from each player: selecting player chooses one for each including self; no courts/King region/Castillo; no fallback stated.

answers.answer: Each affected fellow player secretly selects one region on their disk, simultaneously with the others, and choices are revealed together. A player with a legal region containing at least two of their Caballeros must choose a region containing at least two and return two to the provinces. The King’s region and Castillo cannot be used.
answers.evidence: Fellow players secretly remove two: simultaneous disk selection/reveal; chosen region must contain at least two; never King’s region or Castillo.

answers.answer: If the player has at most one in every legal region, they choose a region containing one and return that one Caballero to the provinces. No procedure is stated if they have no eligible pieces.
answers.evidence: Secretly remove two: ‘If ... at most one in every region, choose a region with one and return that one’; no procedure for no eligible pieces.

answers.answer: Each affected fellow player secretly chooses, on a disk, a region containing at least one of their Caballeros; selections are simultaneous and revealed together. They return all their own Caballeros in that region to the provinces. A player with none in any region is unaffected. The King’s region and Castillo are excluded.
answers.evidence: Secretly remove all: chooses region with at least one, simultaneous secret selection; returns all own there; none in any region unaffected; protected locations excluded.

answers.answer: Yes, the choosing player may select any region, including the King’s region or Castillo. Normal region-scoring rules, rank limits, and applicable bonuses apply. If Castillo is scored, cover the same pieces afterward; do not redistribute them.
answers.evidence: Pick one region to score: any including King’s region/Castillo; normal rules and bonuses; Castillo pieces covered again without redistribution.

answers.answer: The printed 4-value group is Galicia (4/2/0), Catalonia (4/2/1), and Seville (4/3/1). Eligibility is determined by the current first scoreboard value. Galicia with 8/4/0 does not qualify; Granada with 4/0/0 qualifies. Applicable bonuses apply to special scorings.
answers.evidence: All 4-value regions: current first value; Galicia mobile 8/4/0 removes it, Granada 4/0/0 adds it; bonuses apply to special scorings.

answers.answer: The printed 5-value group is Basque Country (5/3/1), Aragon (5/4/1), and Valencia (5/3/2). The printed 6-and-7 group is Old Castile (6/4/2), New Castile (7/4/2), and Granada (6/3/1). A mobile scoreboard replaces printed values, so current first value controls category eligibility. Castillo is explicitly excluded from all-5 scoring.
answers.evidence: Stack 3 lists both printed groups; mobile scoreboard replaces printed values for category eligibility; Castillo not scored in all-5.

answers.answer: Only sole first-place players score; a tie for first scores nothing, because it would ordinarily receive second-place value. Lower ranks score nothing. Castillo is excluded.
answers.evidence: First position only: only sole first places score; tie scores nothing; other ranks nothing; excludes Castillo.

answers.answer: Score both board regions tied for the most. The Castillo is neither considered nor scored, even if it contains more Caballeros than either region.
answers.evidence: Most-Caballeros card: score all regions tied for most; Castillo neither considered nor scored.

answers.answer: Compare nonempty board regions and score all regions tied for the least. Empty regions and the Castillo are neither considered nor scored.
answers.evidence: Least-Caballeros card: compare nonempty board regions; score all tied for least; empty regions and Castillo excluded.

answers.answer: All fellow players move all of their own Caballeros out of the chosen region. Each affected player secretly chooses another region using their disk; choices are revealed simultaneously and their group moves there. If a player chooses the King’s region or the region being vacated, that player’s pieces go to their court instead. The King’s taboo bars taking pieces out of the King’s region, and Castillo cannot be emptied by this card. The summary does not reconcile how the disk’s lack of a Castillo choice applies to this forced movement case.
answers.evidence: Stack 4 Movement gives ownership, all pieces, disk choice and court fallback; edge-case note says source does not reconcile Castillo with disks omitting it.

answers.answer: Royal Adviser moves the King at most one region, into a neighboring region. The King card may put him in any region except the Castillo.
answers.evidence: Royal Adviser: neighboring region, no more than one away; King card: any region except Castillo.

answers.answer: The Court moves two of your own Caballeros from the provinces to your court. This special action is separate from the 4-stack card’s ordinary deployment of up to four from court to the board; complete the two activities separately, in either order.
answers.evidence: The Court: two own from provinces to court; separate from ordinary up-to-four court-to-board deployment; either can go first.

answers.answer: All players secretly choose a region on their disks and reveal simultaneously. The disk allows any of the nine board regions, including the King’s region, but not Castillo. Score each uniquely chosen region under normal rules; a region selected by multiple players is not scored.
answers.evidence: Each secretly chooses a region to score: all choose secretly/reveal simultaneously; duplicate choices do not score; disk excludes Castillo but includes King’s region.

answers.answer: You may take all your own Caballeros from one region and distribute them among other regions and/or the Castillo; you may return some to the original region. Origins exclude the King’s region and Castillo; destinations exclude the King’s region but may include Castillo. Ordinary deployment separately retains its adjacency restriction.
answers.evidence: Intrigue all-own-from-one-region: may return some to original; origins exclude King region/Castillo, destinations exclude King region and may include Castillo.

answers.answer: The two additional Caballeros come from your court and may go to any non-King region and/or Castillo; they do not require adjacency. Including the normal one Caballero deployment, up to three may enter the board, and only the normal one must go adjacent to the King.
answers.evidence: Intrigue two-more-from-court: up to two additional to any non-King destinations; with normal one up to three; only normal one requires adjacency.

answers.answer: No. Choose one of the two special alternatives, not both. The card’s normal deployment of up to one Caballero still applies.
answers.evidence: Intrigue choice card: choose one preceding special action, not both; normal deployment still applies.

answers.answer: Move up to five own and/or foreign Caballeros from one origin region only, distributing them to other non-King regions and/or Castillo. They cannot come from multiple origin regions; the origin itself is not a destination under this card’s ‘other’ restriction.
answers.evidence: Intrigue up to five: own and/or foreign from one origin region, distributed to other non-King regions and/or Castillo.

answers.answer: Move up to three foreign Caballeros only; you may use multiple non-King board-region origins. Your own pieces cannot be included, and pieces cannot come from Castillo. Destinations may be any non-King regions and/or Castillo.
answers.evidence: Intrigue any three foreign: up to three other players’ pieces from any non-King board regions, multiple origins, never Castillo; destinations any non-King regions/Castillo.

answers.answer: The any-three card moves up to three own and/or foreign Caballeros from any non-King origin regions to any non-King regions and/or Castillo. The any-four card moves up to four own and/or foreign from non-King origins to other non-King regions and/or Castillo. The four-piece card’s destination wording is ‘other regions’; the summary notes this difference.
answers.evidence: Intrigue table distinguishes any-three destinations (‘any’) from any-four destinations (‘other’), with maxima and ownership/origin rules.

answers.answer: Move up to two of your own plus up to two foreign Caballeros, as separate ownership allowances. They may come from any regions; however, general relocation origins exclude the King’s region and Castillo. Destinations may be any non-King regions and/or Castillo.
answers.evidence: Intrigue states separate ‘two own plus two foreign’ allowances and ‘from any regions’; general rules say origins exclude King’s region/Castillo and destinations can include Castillo. The summary does not specifically resolve this card’s source wording against the general restrictions.

answers.answer: Move up to four Caballeros, own only, from any non-King origin regions into other non-King regions and/or Castillo. The source and destination restrictions apply; no foreign pieces may be moved.
answers.evidence: Intrigue: any four of your own, up to four own only, from non-King origins into other non-King regions and/or Castillo.

answers.answer: The each-player-secretly-chooses scoring action allows any of the nine board regions, including the King’s region, but not Castillo. By comparison, the choosing player on ‘Pick one region to score’ may choose any region, including both the King’s region and Castillo.
answers.evidence: Stack 4 secret scoring disk: nine board regions including King’s, not Castillo; Stack 2 pick one: any region including King’s or Castillo.

answers.answer: The two mobile scoreboards begin beside the board. The place-or-move action may introduce a scoreboard from beside the board or move one already on the board to a different region.
answers.evidence: Setup places both mobile scoreboards beside board; Stack 4 action allows introducing one or moving one already on board.
